feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It is well written overall, but it feels dense and somewhat repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused evidence beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in leadership roles with meaningful scale: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers.  
- Strong positioning for digital platform, governance, analytics, and multimedia leadership; the profile and skills align well with the experience.  
- Credibility is reinforced by concrete tools, platforms, and recent projects, especially Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, AI search, and studio/video operations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across summary, competencies, skills, and experience; several phrases recur (“governance,” “workflows,” “digital communications,” “AI-enabled”). Tightening would improve clarity and impact.  
- Add more measurable outcomes in multiple roles, not just responsibilities: e.g., growth, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, cost savings, adoption, or turnaround times.  
- Fix stylistic/grammar consistency: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s”; serial comma use is inconsistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. lists without it); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot.” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it would benefit from tighter phrasing and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with a more direct verb structure: “leading/modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance, and content operations.”
- Add one concrete scale cue from recent experience to increase impact, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal platform” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Trim the list of functions to the most differentiating themes: web modernization, analytics/governance, and AI-enabled discovery; multimedia can be secondary.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads Drupal-based web transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” and the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” are somewhat repetitive.
- The long capability list duplicates Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Prioritize strategic, senior-level capabilities over operational phrasing; e.g., use “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “website modernization.”
- Tighten and standardize terms for parallel structure: “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure.”
- Consider a sharper version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space allows, order by strongest differentiators: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, then communications/multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with header, recent projects, and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already covered clearly in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding light outcome/context cues would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action verbs and structure: “Built/Developed/Launched [project] for [audience/purpose], featuring [key elements].”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future campaign expansion”; “bill-level AI chat” to “bill-level AI assistant” if that better matches tone.
- Standardize style and punctuation, including “10 × 20-foot” and consistent use of “AI-enabled.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series closely overlap with Work Experience bullets; consider reframing them as named examples with distinct outcomes or audiences.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “multimedia,” and “campaign” language repeats elsewhere; avoid restating responsibilities already covered in role descriptions.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level impact, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with outcome + scope: “Advise NACo on enterprise web modernization, digital governance, campaign delivery, and content operations for public-facing member communications.”
- Collapse overlapping duties into 3–4 sharper bullets; e.g. “Built Drupal campaign experiences and reusable microsite/toolkit components” and “Improved cross-channel workflows, analytics, and publishing systems supporting organization-wide communications.”
- Emphasize senior advisory language over execution-only phrasing: replace “Deliver CMS development…” with “Led CMS/front-end enhancements and resolved technical issues across large public-facing web properties.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages/templates launched, workflow time reduced, search success uplift, engagement/downloads, or stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance… across web, email, social and multimedia” repeat the 2022–2024 Director role.
- Microsites, AI-enabled search, and campaign storytelling duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level and project list more specific.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and budget oversight across web, email, social, and video.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing, especially for email/social, video studio, and analytics (e.g., engagement growth, production volume, cost savings, reporting speed, adoption by teams).
- Tighten phrasing: replace “along with”/“including” constructions with direct verbs; keep 4–5 bullets max and lead with website modernization, analytics infrastructure, and studio build as the strongest differentiators.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this higher-level and strategic here.
- Governance/publishing standards also echo the current consultant role, so frame this as enterprise operational leadership rather than general best practices.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to the operational scale-up phase and emphasize outcomes, ownership, and team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social, and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable impact where possible: newsletter open/click growth, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of cross-functional teams supported.
- Strengthen action verbs and ownership: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update,” “built cross-team editorial planning processes,” “standardized digital publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this as scaling/distribution rather than initial creation.
- “Improved publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” partially duplicate the 2022–2024 Director entry; keep this version tactical and execution-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tighter and more differentiated, emphasizing strategic leadership rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less duplicative phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with your recent roles.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker than the rest; “Audience-centered content strategy” sounds more senior.
- If space allows, make this category more distinctive by foregrounding governance/operations over broad messaging.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” already closely mirror Core Competencies and the header.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the strongest, most recent items first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, and AI-enabled search; demote older or less central platforms.
- Consider dropping one or two lower-priority platforms here (e.g., SharePoint, Power Pages) unless they are important for target roles.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Drupal modernization for large public-facing sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure, KPI design and executive reporting.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than eight separate fragments.
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with broader, stronger phrasing like “search, content and conversion performance analysis” if accurate.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure and KPI design • Executive reporting and decision-support dashboards • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • Search, content and user-performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” analytics section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave the full tool list in Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” may be weaker than “executive reporting” or “decision-support reporting.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production leadership and event delivery rather than tool-level tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability statement: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to align with the in-house studio achievement in the 2022–2024 role.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” for “Live, hybrid and virtual event production” for clearer scope.
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of generic phrasing, e.g. “Advocacy video programming and event livestream production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- PTZ camera systems is quite tool-specific compared with the rest of the CV; keep only if targeting production-heavy roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent digital leader, this item should emphasize strongest/current platforms and reduce lower-value entries.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance and recency: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level: **Drupal (advanced), WordPress (working), SharePoint/Power Pages (working knowledge), GitHub Pages**
- Consider trimming **GitHub Pages** unless it supports a notable project; it feels less aligned with the enterprise/public-sector positioning.
- Keep punctuation consistent with other technical lists; avoid over-formatting.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**. Consider keeping platforms in one place only, or using this item for depth (e.g., proficiency levels) while the other stays broader.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless tied to a specific platform.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and the more current tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied execution: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling by use case: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3”
- If accurate, add one specificity cue tied to recent work, e.g. “custom Drupal front-end implementation” or “serverless scripting” to better connect with current roles

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills item [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”); avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim
- GTM also relates to analytics/optimization; if space is tight, consider moving it under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” instead

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & collaboration systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/ops platforms: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team coordination: Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier should lead because they align with your recent systems/governance work.
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value collaboration tools if space is tight; too many PM/chat tools can dilute the automation focus.
- If format allows, add a light qualifier: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams overlap with general workplace tools and may add less value than automation-specific platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too generic and underplays the strongest, most recent platform. It should emphasize enterprise email/engagement systems and align with the NACo experience without repeating newsletter management details.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- Consider tightening the label to signal scope: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms** or **CRM & Email Engagement Platforms**
- If accurate, add functional context instead of just names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp**
- If Dynamics 365 was the primary recent system, consider splitting it out for emphasis: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (earlier use)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “newsletters,” “audience growth,” or send-volume claims here; those are already covered in recent work experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this item mostly repeats the “Topline Skills” analytics section and the Director role. It would be stronger if framed around capability depth and outcomes, not just a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and group for clarity: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Tag Manager • SEO analysis • A/B testing • Dashboard development”
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “Dashboard development” or “Executive reporting” for a more professional, outcome-oriented phrasing.
- Add one higher-value capability if accurate, such as “KPI design,” “conversion analysis,” or “behavioral analytics,” to show strategic use beyond tools.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this stack to impact in experience bullets (e.g., reporting for 3.5M annual page views, improved decision-making, optimization insights).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly duplicative of “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping the fuller version in one place only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in concrete outputs or scale.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh, improving publishing coordination and day-to-day digital execution across channels.”
- Tighten multimedia phrasing: “Produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, expanding in-house multimedia capacity.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.” If possible, add volume/frequency metrics for livestreams, videos, or channels supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/early production rather than expansion.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as early team-building and foundational process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize initiative, scope, and any concrete outputs to make it feel distinct.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around innovation/program support plus one standout digital accomplishment: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the second sentence and foreground ownership: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add measurable detail: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or types of materials produced.
- Consider a sharper version: “Supported innovation and policy research projects for county-focused programs while producing digital content and multimedia materials. Launched NACo’s first podcast, owning planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/research support.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
